_note: Every numeric value used by the erythrocyte model. Each carries units, the symbol used in code, a reference key (see references.json), and a short justification. Values are physiologically representative human-RBC values at 37 C; some kinetic constants are rounded/illustrative and are flagged as such. ref keys map into references.json.

V_cyto0.note: Resting red-cell water volume ~90 fL (mean cell volume; water fraction ~0.7 of 130 fL total handled as effective osmotic water).

V_plasma.note: Finite extracellular bath per cell (10x cell volume) so totals are conserved; large enough that bulk plasma is nearly clamped.

Cm.note: Specific membrane capacitance, ~1 uF/cm^2 (used only for Vm dynamics; RBC Vm is solved at quasi-steady state).

Ca.note: Resting free [Ca2+]i ~ 50 nM, kept low by PMCA.

glucose.note: Intracellular glucose (near plasma at rest; GLUT1 near-equilibrative).

X.note: Impermeant intracellular anion (mostly hemoglobin + organic phosphates); amount fixed, concentration computed for electroneutrality at init.

zX.note: Mean valence of the impermeant anion pool at pH 7.2 (effective).

NADH.note: Free NADH (small; most NAD is oxidized).

Imax.note: Max Na+/K+-ATPase turnover (max Na+ efflux; K+ influx = 2/3 of this). ~2-3 mmol Na/L_cell/h, balancing the passive Na+ leak at the resting [Na+]i=10 mM (pump-leak steady state).

P_Na.note: Passive Na+ permeability (GHK). Tuned with pump for resting [Na+]i.

P_K.note: Passive (background) K+ permeability (GHK). Matched to P_Na so the 3:2 pump stoichiometry balances both leaks simultaneously at rest.

P_Cl.note: Very high effective Cl- permeability via Band 3; keeps Cl- near electrochemical equilibrium and sets Vm.

P_Ca.note: Tiny passive Ca2+ leak into the cell, balanced at rest by PMCA; together they set resting [Ca2+]i ~ 50 nM. Both Ca2+ fluxes are small (~uM/L_cell/min) in the RBC.

g_max.note: Max Gardos (KCa3.1) K+ permeability when fully Ca2+-activated.

Imax.note: Max PMCA Ca2+ extrusion rate. Small in absolute terms because RBC Ca2+ turnover is low; high affinity keeps free [Ca2+]i ~ 50 nM. Balanced at rest against the passive Ca2+ leak.

Vmax.note: Max GLUT1 facilitated-diffusion rate (high; transport is near-equilibrative).

k_exchange.note: Effective (normalised) Cl-/HCO3- exchange rate; fast relative to pump-leak so the two anions stay near their equilibrium ratio (electroneutral antiport). Lumped from the very high Band 3 turnover.

Lp.note: Effective osmotic water permeability lumped constant; volume relaxes to osmotic balance fast vs ion changes.

Vmax_HK.note: Lumped upper-glycolysis (hexokinase-limited) flux Vmax; sets overall glucose consumption ~1-2 mmol/L_cell/h scaled.

Km_ATP_gly.note: ATP requirement for upper glycolysis (hexokinase/PFK use ATP).

Km_ADP_gly.note: ADP requirement for the ATP-generating (lower glycolysis) steps; couples flux to ADP supply and bounds the adenine pool.

k_lactate_efflux.note: Lumped lactate clearance (MCT1 export + downstream removal), keeping intracellular lactate near steady state.

f_BPG.note: Fraction of flux diverted through the 2,3-BPG (Rapoport-Luebering) shunt at rest.

k_BPG_deg.note: 2,3-BPG phosphatase turnover returning BPG to the main pathway.

ATP_yield.note: Net ATP per glucose via anaerobic glycolysis (RBC has no mitochondria); BPG shunt bypasses one ATP-generating step.
